chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu al-Mi'za, from Ali, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

key_terms.الْعَقِيقَةُ: Aqiqah, the ritual sacrifice of an animal upon the birth of a child
key_terms.وَاجِبَةٌ: Obligatory, a specific level of legal duty in Shia jurisprudence

ai.seo_question: Is Aqiqah obligatory or recommended in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This concise narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), transmitted via the reliable chain of Ibn Abi Umayr, firmly establishes the obligation (wajib) of 'Aqiqah in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing it from the more common status of sunnah mu'akkadah in other schools. The hadith appears in Chapter 40 of Al-Tusi's *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, a primary source for Shia fiqh, highlighting the ritual's integration into the broader legal framework of family and birth rites. This ruling underscores the communal and spiritual responsibility of parents to express gratitude for the new life through sacrificial offering.
